entities.summary: Jessie Willcox Smith was an American illustrator during the Golden Age of American illustration. She was considered "one of the greatest pure illustrators". A contributor to books and magazines during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Smith illustrated stories and articles for clients such as Century, Collier's, Leslie's Weekly, Harper's, McClure's, Scribners, and the Ladies' Home Journal. She had an ongoing relationship with Good Housekeeping, which included a long-running Mother Goose series of illustrations and also the creation of all the Good Housekeeping covers from December 1917 to 1933.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the greatest pure illustrators of her time, Jessie Willcox Smith's work had a significant regional impact on American culture during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, shaping the visual identity of popular magazines such as Good Housekeeping and influencing generations of illustrators to come.
